name: Why does my bathroom sometimes smell like sewer gas?

mainEntity.name: Why does my bathroom sometimes smell like sewer gas?

acceptedAnswer.text: A sewer gas smell in your bathroom can be caused by several issues. A dry P-trap, which is the U-shaped pipe under your sink or shower, can allow sewer gases to escape if it doesn't have water in it. This often happens in rarely used drains. Other causes include a cracked or improperly sealed toilet wax ring, a clogged or improperly vented drain line, or even a damaged sewer line. Identifying the exact source usually requires a professional inspection to ensure the problem is resolved correctly and to prevent potential health hazards from prolonged exposure to sewer gases.
acceptedAnswer.description: Sewer gas smells can stem from dry P-traps, faulty toilet seals, or issues with drain lines or vents, allowing gases into your home.
